subject: Proposal: 90-day soft-stop window & termination-for-convenience carve-in for pilot migrations
messages:
From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@brightline.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot order — opt-out timing and TFC carve-in question

Mina, thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited. Legal flagged two items in the Order Form/MSA pairing we'd like to resolve before signature: (1) the auto-renew cadence (we need a clearer soft-stop for pilots moving to paid), and (2) an explicit carve-in to allow a one-time termination-for-convenience (TFC) for pilots in the first contract year with a 90-day notice.

Can Redwood propose language that preserves predictable revenue for you while giving Brightline a reasonable rollback path if integration doesn't meet expectations? We're targeting a go/no-go decision window at the 3-month mark.

Attachments: Brightline_Questions.pdf

Thanks,
Sophie Tran
Procurement Lead — Brightline Health

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot order — opt-out timing and TFC carve-in question

Hi Sophie — appreciate the clear ask and the context.

Short answer: we can accommodate a pilot-friendly soft-stop with limited commercial protections for Redwood. Proposed commercial guardrails we typically ask for are: a one-time non-refundable pilot conversion fee (to cover provisioning and reserved capacity), and a 90-day advance notice to terminate for convenience within the first 12 months. After that period the standard auto-renew kicks in.

I'm looping in Ben (sales) and Karthik (legal) to draft specific redline language. Ben — can you confirm acceptable commercial offsets? Karthik — can you propose MSA/Order Form language that: 1) specifies the one-time TFC carve-in for pilot orders only; 2) caps the customer obligation to the pilot conversion fee + any unpaid usage through the 90-day notice; and 3) preserves Redwood's standard auto-renew thereafter.

I'll attach our suggested Order Form template with comment placeholders.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Sales Ops — Redwood Inference

Sophie / Mina — quick commercial note from Sales: we can accept the 90-day pilot TFC with the following commercial offsets: (a) one-time pilot setup fee of $15k, (b) minimum committed usage for the pilot month (prorated token commitments) to cover GPU allocation, and (c) a requirement that the TFC applies only once per account (i.e., one pilot carve-in per customer during first contract year).

If that sounds reasonable we can reflect it in the Order Form and still keep the hosted pricing bands unchanged for the remainder of the term.

Mina — I'll prepare a clean Order Form + short summary memo for legal to sign off. Sophie — are you ok with the one-time setup fee?

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot order — opt-out timing and TFC carve-in question

Folks — attaching proposed redline language below (and in attached doc). High level commentary and why it protects Redwood while granting Brightline the pilot flexibility requested: 

--- Proposed (MSA / Order Form language snippet) ---
1) Pilot carve-in: For any Order Form designated as a “Pilot Order” the parties agree that Customer may exercise a one-time Termination for Convenience within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date of that Order Form by providing at least ninety (90) days’ prior written notice. Such termination shall only be available once per Customer account.

2) Financial consequences: If Customer exercises the one-time Termination for Convenience under Section 1 above, Customer shall be obligated to pay: (a) the non-refundable Pilot Setup Fee set forth in the applicable Order Form; (b) all unpaid charges for usage incurred through the effective date of termination; and (c) any reasonably documented third-party costs directly incurred by Redwood in provisioning dedicated capacity for the Pilot (not to exceed the total Pilot Setup Fee).

3) Effect on auto-renew: Unless otherwise set forth in the applicable Order Form, the Term of each Order Form shall automatically renew for successive periods as set forth therein. The one-time Termination for Convenience rights in Section 1 are a limited carve-in and do not otherwise modify the automatic renewal provisions of the MSA for non-pilot Orders.

4) Good faith cooperation: Parties agree to cooperate in good faith to coordinate offboarding tasks (data export, KV cache handoff, and scheduled capacity deprovisioning) during the 90-day notice window. Redwood will provide standard offboarding documentation and up to two (2) hours of technical assistance during the notice period at no charge; additional services will be billed at standard professional services rates.

--- end snippet ---

Comments: this language is intentionally narrow, caps Redwood exposure (non-refundable fee + unpaid usage + documented provisioning costs), and sets expectations around offboarding. I recommend we (a) put the Pilot Setup Fee and the committed usage numbers into the Order Form table, and (b) add a carve-out that TFC cannot be used to avoid payment of amounts already due under the Order Form.

Next steps: Mina / Ben — please confirm the Pilot Setup Fee and committed minimum. Sophie / Tom — if Brightline approves the narrow carve-in, I'll produce a tracked-redline MSA + Order Form and upload to DocuSign (link below) for signatures.

DocuSign link (draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BRG-1472-sign
